messages:
Maria Lopez: heads up — hit a weird double-apply during a tenant move + eviction interleave on staging earlier. logging + short reproduction below. 
Maria Lopez: ```
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z [node-12] lease revoke prefix=tenants/42/conv epoch=128 holder=node-12
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z [node-12] eviction start prefix=tenants/42/conv reason=memory_pressure
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z [node-11] acquire lease prefix=tenants/42/conv epoch=129 holder=node-11
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z [node-11] apply handoff incoming-prefix-state=hot
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z [node-12] eviction complete prefix=tenants/42/conv status=removed
2026-03-15T14:02:03Z [node-11] apply double-apply-detected prefix=tenants/42/conv
```
Maria Lopez: repro script: `./scripts/repro-interleave.sh --ten=42 --delay-evict 5ms`

Devin K.: ack. can you repro reliably? interleave window looks tiny.

Maria Lopez: about 90% on the 5ms weave on my small harness. bigger cluster -> rarer but still shows up under stress.

Samir Nair: quick theory: eviction comparator uses timestamp of local eviction commit + best-effort lease revoke ordering. if handoff and eviction are concurrent, we can lose a deterministic ordering and both nodes think they should apply. essentially a compare() that isn't total.

Rachel P.: are we sure it's not just eventual duplicate apply that's idempotent? we should confirm side-effects (we saw two writes to downstream metadatastore).

Maria Lopez: confirmed — downstream got two different "applied_by" tags and metrics counted prefix-residency twice. not idempotent in current code path.

Jia Chen: possible fixes (brainstorm):
- make eviction/handoff comparator total and deterministic: compare(lease_epoch, handoff_serial, node_id) so ties break consistently across nodes.
- attach a monotonic handoff_serial from sequencer/KV-manager when a handoff intent is created.
- make apply operation check a canonical token in downstream store and reject if already applied (idempotency at sink).
- short-term: introduce a small randomized jitter to eviction completion so two nodes less likely to finish same microsecond (hacky).

Samir Nair: prefer deterministic comparator + handoff_serial. jitter is brittle. idempotency at sink is good belt-and-suspenders but we need to avoid both nodes attempting heavy work concurrently (cost + race).

Devin K.: caveat: adding handoff_serial requires sequencer involvement for every handoff intent — perf/regression risk. can we derive a serial from existing lease epoch + prefix-hash? e.g., (lease_epoch, hash(prefix) mod 1024, node_id) to be deterministic without extra RPCs?

Jia Chen: hmm hash gives determinism but not monotonicity — two different handoffs could have same hash slot and cause ordering anomalies when epoch equal. but in practice epochs differ when ownership actually changes. still, we shouldn't rely on probabilistic uniqueness.

Rachel P.: another option: piggyback a small monotonic counter on the current lease object (we already update lease metadata on changes). increment counter when we initiate handoff. that stays local to lease record and replicates via the existing lease update path. cheap RPC surface.

Maria Lopez: that sounds promising — lease record already goes through consensus path. adding a `handoff_seq` integer keeps changes local to the lease document and gives us total ordering: compare(lease_epoch, handoff_seq, node_id).

Samir Nair: operational questions: how do we handle stale nodes that replay an old handoff_seq? comparator should treat higher epoch first, then higher handoff_seq, then node id. old nodes with older epoch won't win. make sure handoff_seq is persisted atomically with lease transition.

Devin K.: ok but we must carefully document invariants: handoff_seq only increments when creating a new handoff intent and is part of the atomic lease update. consumer code must read lease metadata before applying prefix state. add defensive check: apply if lease matches (epoch, handoff_seq) you observed; else abort and re-fetch.

Jia Chen: telemetry plan: emit metric `eviction_interleave_detected` with labels (prefix_shard, tenant, node_winner, node_loser) when we detect double-apply or when comparator decision changed during final compare. add debug trace that records (epoch, handoff_seq, comparator_result) for postmortem.

Maria Lopez: quick test plan:
1) add handoff_seq to lease record and comparator change behind a feature flag `eviction_tiebreak_v2`
2) run repro harness with flag on across 50 runs, assert zero double-applies and check latency/regression.
3) enable idempotency guard at downstream as extra safety for canary.

ops-bot: deploy check: feature flag created: `eviction_tiebreak_v2` (off) — owner: @Maria Lopez.

Rachel P.: can someone open a small RFC/PR with code sketch and test harness? I can help with the telemetry bits.

Maria Lopez: I'll open RFC + PR by EOD with benchmark numbers and the test harness changes. tagging @Devin K. and @Samir Nair for review. :thumbsup:

Samir Nair: sounds good. if we do this right we remove the need for downstream complicated idempotency in many places.

Devin K.: ack, will review. also please include a short section on rollback plan if we see regressions in lease update latency.

Maria Lopez: yes — will include rollback toggle + phased canary in prod. thanks all.
